what_its_for: Terbinafine is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the nails (fingernails or toenails) and skin. It works by killing the fungus that causes the infection. It is most commonly prescribed for nail fungus (onychomycosis) and ringworm infections that have not responded to creams or other treatments.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food — it does not matter. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay to do so.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is one 250 mg tablet once a day. For toenail fungus, treatment typically lasts 12 weeks. For fingernail fungus, treatment is usually 6 weeks. For skin infections, your doctor may prescribe a shorter course. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly — do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store terbinafine tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking terbinafine, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. Do not take over-the-counter antacids within 2 hours of your dose, as they may reduce how well the medicine works. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, including herbal supplements, because terbinafine can interact with many drugs, including antidepressants, blood thinners, and heart medicines. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen if needed, as some people may become more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine or pale-colored stools, severe stomach pain or nausea, unusual tiredness or loss of appetite (these may be signs of liver problems); a skin rash, blistering, or peeling; changes in your sense of taste or loss of taste; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; mood changes, depression, or anxiety; or if your infection does not seem to be improving after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Terbinafine works slowly because nails grow slowly. You may not see visible improvement in your nails for several months, even after you finish the full course of treatment. For toenails, it can take 6 to 12 months after finishing the medicine to see a fully healthy nail grow in. For skin infections, you may start to feel better within a few weeks. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment even if you feel better early, to make sure the infection is completely cleared.
special_populations: Liver or kidney problems: Terbinafine is NOT recommended if you have active or chronic liver disease. Your doctor should check your liver function before starting and may monitor it during treatment. If you have moderate to severe kidney disease, your doctor may adjust your dose or recommend a different treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults can generally take this medicine at the same dose, but should be monitored more closely for side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Terbinafine is generally not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. Children: Use in children under 12 years old should only be done under close medical supervision, as dosing will be different based on the child's weight.
